preamble: The shift from the rhotic [r] to the glottal fricative [h] is a form of debuccalization: the trill loses its oral articulation and only glottal friction remains. In most of Brazil the strong R, historically an alveolar trill, is now [h] (rato [ˈhatu]). Balinese turned Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *R into h (*Rumaq 'house' > humah), and Lao has h for Proto-Tai *r (*roːkᴰ 'squirrel' > ຮອກ [hɔːk̚]). Coda debuccalization of the Caribbean Spanish tap is filed under ɾ → h.

examples.note: The from-form is the conservative alveolar trill of the strong R (word-initial and written rr). It has become a glottal or uvular fricative in most of Brazil.
PMP *R is the reconstructed uvular rhotic; in casual speech this h is often dropped (baas).
Thai keeps r: กระรอก.
